justification: Adds the project's finish line for outreach and wires it into CI, and changes public copy on nine surfaces (two claims retired, one published count corrected). A gate that can pass while a public claim is false would re-create the exact failure the outreach hold exists for; a CI step that is wrong blocks or silently waves through every PR.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-09-14 on origin/main: .claude/dq_checks.json held 104 DQ rows and 0 OC- rows; scripts/dq_check.py had no --outreach. The spec (ce-outreach-readiness-benchmark-SPEC-2026-09-11.md) was written 2026-09-11 and never built. The user confirmed the claim set on 2026-09-14 (17 rows, 14 and 15 retired, 17 added). dcpFullCouncils rendered on 7 surfaces plus a 'Full structured DCP' coverage label in DCPInterestForm; the planner page carried a before/after time table. Live: 19 active woollahra registry chapters point at a repealed-plan source; dcpSetbackTripleCouncils was published as 23 and measures 22.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: dq_check.py reads DQ ids from the markdown tracker and fails on any JSON row the tracker lacks, so claim rows could not simply be added. Claim rows backed by a bare 'python' argv ran under a different interpreter found on PATH and errored on collection (OC-16 on the first run). DQ-99's check is its own script, not a dq_probe_live.py id. The retired label also survived inside a JSX comment and a form heading that a surface-level grep of coverage.ts usages did not reach.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses the ledger's machinery rather than a new tracker: OC- rows live in dq_checks.json and use run_one's enforcement; 'true'/'false' join 'fixed'/'open' in _ENFORCED; the ledger coverage check and the three caps skip OC- rows. New: _outreach() (the stop signal), verify_coverage_stats.py --field, and scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py, which composes the DQ ledger's own recorded checks, existing test files and the served read (fetch_dcp_setbacks) for claims no single command answers.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The sources are the production database (read-only via dq_db.connect), the DQ probes and the test suites. A database or probe that cannot run returns UNKNOWN (exit 2), never a pass; a jest-backed part returns UNKNOWN where node_modules is absent. A query that no longer runs, a pytest collection error and a missing ledger row are FAIL, so a broken check is visible. The CI step accepts exit 2 only because its job has no node_modules; done is exit 0 where every check can run.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No API or type contract changes. COVERAGE and COVERAGE_DISPLAY lose the dcpFullCouncils key and change dcpSetbackTripleCouncils to 22 / '22'; every former reader was edited in this branch, so a missed reference fails tsc at pre-commit. The planner page's TIME_SAVINGS array became LOOKUPS with no before/after fields, and its JSX no longer reads them.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Before: a public page could say '7 councils with full structured provisions', '10 minutes, not 2 hours' or '23 councils with front, side and rear setbacks' with nothing able to fail. If the gate were wrong in the permissive direction, outreach would be judged ready while a claim is false; it cannot exit 0 with any claim declared false, unchecked, contradicted or unverified, and the tests force each case. In the strict direction, CI fails only on a contradiction between a declared state and its check.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_dq_check_outreach.py tests/test_dq_check.py tests/test_coverage_source_derived_stats.py -q -o addopts= && python scripts/dq_check.py --outreach
falsifiable_check.fails_when: _outreach returns 0 while any blocking claim is declared false, has no check, is contradicted or could not be verified; a claim declared true whose check fails, or declared false whose check passes, is not reported as a contradiction (exit 1); a row that does not block outreach changes the result; OC rows are reported as ledger orphans or counted in the DQ caps; verify_coverage_stats --field accepts an unknown key or checks fields it was not asked for; a retired phrase renders anywhere under frontend-nextjs app, components or lib; dcpFullCouncils reappears in coverage.ts; or the committed claim set is not OC-1..OC-17 with every row blocking outreach and carrying a check or a reason.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Forced in tests: each exit code (0, 1, 2, 3) is produced by in-memory rows, and run_one returns RED for 'true' + failing and 'false' + passing. On real data the first full run declared every row false and reported 7 CONTRADICTED (OC-1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 11, 15), proving the both-way enforcement bites before those rows were set true. verify_coverage_stats.py --field nope exits 1; --field dcpSetbackTripleCouncils reported 'published 23 vs live 22' (DRIFT), corrected here. The first run also exposed three defects in the gate itself, each fixed and re-run: OC-16 errored under a PATH interpreter (now sys.executable; a collection error is FAIL), OC-17 called DQ-99 through the wrong script (now every DQ part runs the ledger's own check), and OC-14 still found 'Full structured DCP' in DCPInterestForm.tsx (reworded). tests/test_dq_check.py initially failed test_no_orphan_entries and test_the_three_ratchets_measure_different_sets on the new rows; both now exclude OC- rows. 49 targeted tests pass; full suite 6,333 passed with one failure that was a mid-run edit of dq_checks.json and passes alone. The second full run then reported OC-16 CONTRADICTED again: dq_check.run_one itself launched the composite with the PATH python, so the fix inside outreach_claim_checks.py never took effect. run_one now substitutes sys.executable for a bare python argv, for every row.
falsifiable_check.measured: Third full run against production, final state of this branch: 9 of 17 claims pass (OC-1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 11, 14, 15, 16), 8 not yet (OC-4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13, 17 honestly declared false; OC-12 no check), 0 not verified, 0 contradicted; exit 3. Second full run against production after the fixes: 7 of 17 claims passed with 2 contradictions, both explained and fixed in this branch (OC-14 now holds and is declared true; OC-16 failed only through the PATH interpreter). First full run against production, rows then all declared false: 7 checks passed, 9 failed honestly, OC-12 has no check, OC-16 errored (fixed; 123 calibration tests pass). Failing parts: OC-4 DQ-76/78/97/29; OC-6 DQ-96; OC-7 production depth delivery unobserved; OC-8 79 of 837 served numbers lack a clause, sentence or PDF link, plus DQ-39; OC-10 DQ-61 and DQ-70; OC-13 riskLayers ungrounded; OC-17 DQ-66, DQ-32c, DQ-61, DQ-70, 19 repealed-plan chapters, 32 ranges printed as a maximum.

functions.name: _outreach
functions.input: No arguments; it loads every OC- row with blocks_outreach true from .claude/dq_checks.json and runs each row's check through run_one.
functions.output: Exit 0 when every blocking claim is declared true and passes; 1 on any contradiction; 2 when something could not be verified and nothing contradicted; 3 when the file is consistent but claims are declared false or unchecked. Prints one line per claim and a pass count.
functions.if_none: No blocking rows at all returns 1, not 0; a row with no check is never counted as passing.

functions.name: run_one
functions.input: A row id, the row's spec dict with its declared state and check argv, and a verbose flag for single-row runs.
functions.output: A verdict (OK, RED, NO-CHECK, UNKNOWN, ERROR) and detail; 'true' and 'false' are now enforced like 'fixed' and 'open', with their own RED wording.
functions.if_none: A missing check returns NO-CHECK; exit 2 from the check returns UNKNOWN, never a pass.

functions.name: main
functions.input: A single claim id such as OC-8 from the command line, which must be one of the composite claims defined in CLAIMS.
functions.output: Runs every sub-check for that claim, prints PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN per part, exits 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail, 2 if none fail and any could not run.
functions.if_none: An unknown or missing claim id prints usage and exits 1.

functions.name: probe
functions.input: A DQ id whose recorded check in .claude/dq_checks.json should be run exactly as the ledger runs it.
functions.output: PASS on exit 0, FAIL on exit 1, UNKNOWN otherwise, with the probe's last output line.
functions.if_none: A missing ledger row or a row with no check is FAIL, so a claim cannot pass on a probe that does not exist.

functions.name: served_entries
functions.input: No arguments; it opens a read-only connection and reads every served council's controls through conveyancing_db.fetch_dcp_setbacks.
functions.output: A list of (lga, entry, registry_pdf_urls) for every served control, as the product serves it, or None with a reason.
functions.if_none: An unreachable database or a failing serve path returns None, which the callers report as UNKNOWN.

functions.name: no_rendered_phrase
functions.input: A label and a case-insensitive regex describing a retired public claim that must not render anywhere on the site.
functions.output: PASS when no non-comment line under frontend-nextjs app, components or lib matches; FAIL with the first matching locations otherwise.
functions.if_none: Lines starting with //, *, /* or {/* are ignored; everything else counts.

functions.name: main
functions.input: Optional argv; --field followed by COVERAGE keys limits the check to those published figures, as the outreach claim rows need.
functions.output: The same drift report as before for the selected keys; exit 0 current, 1 drift or an unknown key, 2 database unreachable.
functions.if_none: argv None means no options (tests call main() under pytest); an unknown key exits 1 before connecting.

real_layer_exempt.scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py: Run in full against the production database (read-only, dq_db.connect) on 2026-09-14, twice: every composite claim executed its SQL, the served read and the DQ ledger's own checks; results are recorded in falsifiable_check.measured. The pure logic (exit-code mapping, phrase scan) is exercised by those runs and by tests/test_dq_check_outreach.py through dq_check.
real_layer_exempt.scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py: tests/test_verify_coverage_stats_real_db.py (database-marked) already exercises main() against the live catalog; main() keeps its no-argument behaviour for it. The new --field mode was run live and reported the real 23-vs-22 drift.
real_layer_exempt.scripts/dq_check.py: The new code runs subprocess checks, not a database or HTTP call of its own; tests/test_dq_check_outreach.py forces every exit code and the both-way enforcement with real subprocesses in run_one.

values.value: Each OC- row's declared state ('true', 'false' or 'unverifiable') and blocks_outreach flag in .claude/dq_checks.json
values.if_missing: A row without blocks_outreach is ignored by the stop signal; a missing declared state is not enforced and the claim cannot count as passing.

values.value: The published COVERAGE integers in frontend-nextjs/lib/coverage.ts, including dcpSetbackTripleCouncils now 22
values.if_missing: A key absent from COVERAGE is reported as drift and exits 1.

values.value: The check argv the DQ ledger records for DQ-29, 32c, 39, 50, 61, 66, 70, 76, 78, 96, 97 and 99
values.if_missing: A missing row or null check is FAIL for that part of the claim.

queries.purpose: Every served council, so the served read can be run for each and its citations and range wording checked
queries.where_clause: is_current AND (needs_review IS NULL OR needs_review = FALSE) AND lga <> 'nsw_statewide' AND lga <> 'inner_west'

queries.purpose: Councils whose LEP zones are all marked complete, for the permitted-uses claim
queries.where_clause: GROUP BY lga HAVING bool_and(is_complete) -- counted, must equal 26

queries.purpose: Active registry chapters sourced from a repealed-plan archive, for the plan-in-force claim
queries.where_clause: is_active AND (council_url ILIKE '%repealed%' OR r2_current_path ILIKE '%repealed%' OR r2_public_pdf_url ILIKE '%repealed%')

queries.purpose: The existing published-coverage queries, now filterable per field
queries.where_clause: unchanged per-field queries in QUERIES; --field only selects which run

break_it.scenario: A row is edited to declared 'true' while its check still fails, to make the pass count look better.
break_it.what_happens: Outreach would be judged ready on a false claim.
break_it.how: run_one returns RED for 'true' + failing; _outreach exits 1 and the CI step in the database job fails on exit 1. Forced in test_run_one_enforces_true_and_false_both_ways and test_a_contradicted_claim_fails_whatever_else_is_true.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/test_dq_check_outreach.py -k "both_ways or contradicted" -q -o addopts=

break_it.scenario: The database is unreachable, or jest's node_modules are absent, so some claim checks cannot run.
break_it.what_happens: A gate that folded 'could not look' into pass would report ready without looking.
break_it.how: Exit 2 from any part is UNKNOWN; _outreach returns 2 and never 0. test_could_not_verify_is_never_ready forces it.

break_it.scenario: A council's numbers are served under a slug the served-council query skips (scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py:131, WHERE is_current AND (needs_review IS NULL OR needs_review = FALSE) AND lga <> 'nsw_statewide' AND lga <> 'inner_west').
break_it.what_happens: OC-8 and OC-17 would never read that council's served numbers and could pass while they are uncited or wrongly scoped.
break_it.how: Measured 2026-09-14: inner_west holds 0 served numbers (its three former councils are served under their own slugs, which the query includes) and nsw_statewide is the statewide pseudo-council the published counts also exclude.
break_it.repro: SELECT lga, count(*) FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE is_current AND (needs_review IS NULL OR needs_review = FALSE) AND lga IN ('inner_west','nsw_statewide') GROUP BY lga

break_it.scenario: A council repeals its plan without the word 'repealed' in any URL we hold (scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py:291, WHERE is_active AND (council_url ILIKE '%repealed%' OR r2_current_path ILIKE '%repealed%' OR r2_public_pdf_url ILIKE '%repealed%')), as Strathfield did.
break_it.what_happens: That part of OC-17 passes while numbers from a repealed plan are served.
break_it.how: Not caught by this query. It is one of the eight UNKNOWN items recorded in the spec §10 (oldest plan dates and the unmonitored councils) whose one measurement is a check of each council's policy page; until measured, OC-17 also fails on DQ-61 and DQ-70, so the gate cannot be ready.

break_it.scenario: A council is added to lep_zone_coverage, or loses a zone's is_complete flag (scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py:259, GROUP BY lga HAVING bool_and(is_complete)).
break_it.what_happens: The published 'permitted uses for 26 councils' would silently become an under- or overstatement.
break_it.how: The part requires exactly 26, so drift in either direction fails OC-11, which is declared true; the CI step then fails on the contradiction.

break_it.scenario: A retired claim ('full structured provisions', '10 minutes, not 2 hours', before/after minutes) is re-added to a page, component or lib file.
break_it.what_happens: The site would repeat a claim the user decided to stop making.
break_it.how: OC-14 and OC-15 scan every non-comment line under frontend-nextjs app, components and lib; the first run caught a surviving 'Full structured DCP' heading the usage grep missed. test_the_retired_full_councils_figure_stays_retired guards coverage.ts.
break_it.repro: python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-14 && python scripts/outreach_claim_checks.py OC-15

break_it.scenario: A claim check runs under the wrong Python interpreter and its test file errors on collection.
break_it.what_happens: Observed on the first run for OC-16; had a collection error been read as 'unknown' or 'pass', a validated claim would be unverifiable or a broken one would pass.
break_it.how: Composite parts use sys.executable, and any non-zero pytest exit (1, 2, 4, 5) is FAIL; only a process that cannot start is UNKNOWN.

break_it.scenario: A claim's part points at a DQ probe that does not exist or has no check.
break_it.what_happens: Observed for DQ-99 on the first run (wrong script, reported 'could not look'); a silent skip would let OC-17 pass without that evidence.
break_it.how: probe() runs the ledger's own recorded argv for the id, and a missing row or null check is FAIL.

break_it.scenario: Work on the red claims finishes and the gate exits 0 while the UNKNOWN items from the 2026-09-14 disposition (old plan dates, DQ-33, retired zone codes, DQ-69/88, DQ-85, DQ-58, unaudited pages, Threat Radar wording) were never measured.
break_it.what_happens: The gate would report ready on claims whose evidence has a known, unmeasured gap.
break_it.how: Recorded, not automated: each needs one bounded measurement (spec §10) and then joins a claim's check or gets a one-line reason. The spec rule is that an UNKNOWN may not survive two sessions.

break_it.scenario: dq_check.run_one launches a row whose argv starts with a bare 'python' on a machine where PATH resolves to a different interpreter than the one running the gate.
break_it.what_happens: Observed for OC-16 on the second run: the shadow calibration test errored on collection under the other venv, so a validated claim read as contradicted.
break_it.how: run_one replaces a bare python/python3 argv[0] with sys.executable before running any check; in CI the two are identical.

break_it.scenario: A claim row names the wrong COVERAGE key, so the per-field run of the existing coverage queries (scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py:247, the unchanged per-field queries in QUERIES now filterable per field) checks an unrelated figure and passes.
break_it.what_happens: The claim would read as verified on a number it does not state; an unknown or misspelt key could also silently check nothing.
break_it.how: --field rejects any key that is not checkable before connecting (exit 1, observed with --field nope), and each OC row's claim text names the COVERAGE keys its check passes so a mismatch is visible in review; the published-figure test_every_published_number_is_checked_by_something still covers every key.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: on main, with frontend node_modules present, run python scripts/dq_check.py --outreach and confirm exit 3 with the pass count reported in the PR; confirm the new gates.yml step passes on the merge commit; open /for/planners (no before/after times), /what-you-get (no 'Full structured DCP' tile) and /assessment's DCP coverage panel ('DCP rule text').
